AdjacentGeometry_0.0000

Draws a light grey 400x200 background, then a 4x2 grid of adjacent 100x100 green quads, each offset by the bias in x and y, through a passthrough vertex shader. Grey seams between neighboring quads show inconsistent rounding of shared edges. This case uses no offset.

As AdjacentGeometry_0.0000 with a bias of 0.0010 (a tiny offset).

As AdjacentGeometry_0.0000 with a bias of 0.4999 (just under half a pixel).

As AdjacentGeometry_0.0000 with a bias of 0.5000 (exactly half a pixel).

Compositing_-2

As Compositing_-4, but the final full screen quad is drawn at z = -2.

Compositing_-4

Fills a framebuffer sized texture with a centered 256x256 checkerboard, points the color surface at that texture and draws the left half of the texture onto itself four times through a passthrough vertex shader, with the combiner outputting the texture's color and half its alpha. The texture is then drawn to the screen with a fixed function full screen quad at z = -4. Any offset or blurring in the left half shows texel misalignment that accumulates over the repeated self compositing.

Compositing_2

As Compositing_-4, but the final full screen quad is drawn at z = 2.

Geometry_0.0000

Draws a 240x240 magenta quad centered on the screen, then a green quad over it whose top and left edges are offset by the bias (the right and bottom edges are unchanged), both through a passthrough vertex shader. Any magenta left visible along the top or left edge shows how the offset edge was snapped to the 1/16 subpixel grid and rasterized. This case uses no offset.

GeometrySubscreen_0.0000

For each of four sizes (128x128, 128x32, 32x128 and 16x64), points the color surface at texture memory sized exactly to the quad, fills it with magenta on the CPU and draws a green quad covering the whole surface offset by the bias in x and y through a passthrough vertex shader. Each result is then drawn to the screen as a texture in a 2x2 grid. Magenta shows texels the offset quad did not cover. This case uses no offset.

GeometrySuperscreen_0.0000

As GeometrySubscreen, but the color surface is always 1024x1024 and only the first width * height texels of it (contiguously, not as a rectangle) are filled with magenta before drawing the offset green quad of each size. The top left width x height region of the surface is drawn to the screen for each size. This case uses no offset.

ProjAdjacentGeometry_0.0000

As AdjacentGeometry, but positions are unprojected through a D3D style perspective projection with z varying from the top to the bottom of each quad. Quads alternate in a checkerboard between the programmable pipeline (dark green, 0xFF009900) and the fixed function pipeline (light green, 0xFF00BB00), so seams between them show differences in how the two pipelines round projected vertices. This case uses no offset.

RenderTarget

Points the color surface at a 128x128 render target that is prefilled with translucent magenta, sets the viewport offset to (320.53125, 240.53125) and the viewport scale to (320, -240, 16777215), and draws a quad from (-1, 1) to (1, -1) with a manually loaded vertex program ending in the XDK screen space epilogue (MUL by c[58], RCC of w, MAD with c[59]). The render target is then drawn to the screen with the fixed function pipeline. Magenta shows texels the quad did not cover.

TopLeftRaster

Tests the rasterizer's top-left fill rule and 1/16 subpixel snapping through a passthrough vertex shader. Draws thin vertical quads and triangles whose left edges sit at x + 0.5 (or the next float below it) and step by 1/16 pixel, a 0.2 pixel wide quad that should be invisible without multisampling, quads stacked to share edges at x + 0.5625, black to white horizontal gradient quads whose expected interpolated colors are 0x808080, 0x808080 and 0x000000 from top to bottom, and the same edge patterns rotated to horizontal on the right side of the screen.

TopLeftRaster_Fixed

As TopLeftRaster, but the geometry is drawn through the fixed function pipeline with identity model view and projection matrices and a zero viewport scale and offset.
